name: Lamech
charge: Taking two wives, the first in scripture; killing a man and boasting of it; claiming seventy-sevenfold vengeance
summary: Lamech of Cain’s line was the first man in scripture to take two wives. His house carried the trades of that line, the harp and the organ in one son and the working of brass and iron in another, which is the first making of weapons. He boasted to his wives that he had killed a man, with the weapon his own son had made, and claimed seventy and sevenfold against Cain’s sevenfold. He knew the commandment against killing and appealed past it. No sentence is recorded.
offenseFull: Lamech took two wives, Adah and Zillah (Genesis 4:19). This is the first time scripture records a man taking multiple wives, and it is the sons of the wicked who did it; in the beginning it was one wife, and the line of Seth in the next chapter is not read of doing so (Genesis 2:24; Genesis 5:3-5). His house carried the trades of Cain’s line. Jabal fathered such as dwell in tents and have cattle, Jubal fathered all such as handle the harp and the organ, and Zillah bare Tubalcain, an instructor of every craftsman in brass and iron, which is the first making of weapons (Genesis 4:20-22). Music and warfare both sat in that one household, and the Most High takes the credit for neither man but for the making: he says he created the smith that blows the coals and brings forth an instrument for his work, and created the waster to destroy (Isaiah 54:16).

Lamech told his wives that he had slain a man to his wounding and a young man to his hurt (Genesis 4:23). He did it with what was to hand, and what was to hand was what his own son had forged. He knew the commandment against killing was in force in his day; that is exactly why he appealed to Cain’s sevenfold and claimed seventy and sevenfold for himself (Genesis 4:24; Genesis 4:15). They knew the commandments in that time. The word the Most High had spoken to restrain bloodshed was turned into a man’s boast of his own vengeance, though vengeance belongs to the Lord (Deuteronomy 32:35; Romans 12:19). What he was announcing is the rule his line has kept ever since: touch one of us and we answer seventy times over, a household or a whole city for one man, because we hold the weapons.
judgmentFull: Genesis records no sentence upon this Lamech. His speech stands as the testimony of Cain’s line, growing in violence and self-exaltation, before the account turns to Seth and to those who began to call upon the name of the Lord (Genesis 4:25-26). Two lines carry the same names and not the same spirit. Cain’s Lamech fathered a son of destruction; Seth’s Lamech fathered Noah, and named him for the comfort he would bring concerning their work and the toil of their hands, because of the ground the Lord had cursed (Genesis 5:28-29). Good is set against evil, and life against death, and all the works of the Most High are two and two, one against another (Ecclesiasticus 33:14-15). The line of Cain went on in wickedness until the sons of God mingled with it, the earth was filled with violence, and the flood came (Genesis 6:1-5; Wisdom of Solomon 10:3-4). The absence of a narrated punishment does not turn his claim into God’s promise; delay is not acquittal.

lawsResolved.text: Avenge not yourselves, for vengeance is in God's hands.
All boasting and bragging is wicked.
The restitution and punishment should be according to the crime--Life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, wound for wound, stripe for stripe.

text.text: And Lamech took unto him two wives: the name of the one was Adah, and the name of the other Zillah.
Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh.
And Adam lived an hundred and thirty years, and begat a son in his own likeness, after his image; and called his name Seth:
And the days of Adam after he had begotten Seth were eight hundred years: and he begat sons and daughters:
And all the days that Adam lived were nine hundred and thirty years: and he died.
And Adah bare Jabal: he was the father of such as dwell in tents, and of such as have cattle.
And his brother’s name was Jubal: he was the father of all such as handle the harp and organ.
And Zillah, she also bare Tubal–cain, an instructer of every artificer in brass and iron: and the sister of Tubal–cain was Naamah.
Behold, I have created the smith that bloweth the coals in the fire, and that bringeth forth an instrument for his work; and I have created the waster to destroy.
And Lamech said unto his wives, Adah and Zillah, Hear my voice; ye wives of Lamech, hearken unto my speech: for I have slain a man to my wounding, and a young man to my hurt.
If Cain shall be avenged sevenfold, truly Lamech seventy and sevenfold.
And the Lord said unto him, Therefore whosoever slayeth Cain, vengeance shall be taken on him sevenfold. And the Lord set a mark upon Cain, lest any finding him should kill him.
To me belongeth vengeance, and recompence; their foot shall slide in due time: for the day of their calamity is at hand, and the things that shall come upon them make haste.
Dearly beloved, avenge not yourselves, but rather give place unto wrath: for it is written, Vengeance is mine; I will repay, saith the Lord.
And Adam knew his wife again; and she bare a son, and called his name Seth: For God, said she, hath appointed me another seed instead of Abel, whom Cain slew.
And to Seth, to him also there was born a son; and he called his name Enos: then began men to call upon the name of the Lord.
And Lamech lived an hundred eighty and two years, and begat a son:
And he called his name Noah, saying, This same shall comfort us concerning our work and toil of our hands, because of the ground which the Lord hath cursed.
Good is set against evil, and life against death: so is the godly against the sinner, and the sinner against the godly.
So look upon all the works of the most High; and there are two and two, one against another.
And it came to pass, when men began to multiply on the face of the earth, and daughters were born unto them,
That the sons of God saw the daughters of men that they were fair; and they took them wives of all which they chose.
And the Lord said, My spirit shall not always strive with man, for that he also is flesh: yet his days shall be an hundred and twenty years.

There were giants in the earth in those days; and also after that, when the sons of God came in unto the daughters of men, and they bare children to them, the same became mighty men which were of old, men of renown.
And God saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and that every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually.
But when the unrighteous went away from her in his anger, he perished also in the fury wherewith he murdered his brother.
For whose cause the earth being drowned with the flood, wisdom again preserved it, and directed the course of the righteous in a piece of wood of small value.
And Zillah, she also bare Tubal–cain, an instructer of every artificer in brass and iron: and the sister of Tubal–cain was Naamah.
